headline-lg.purpose: Large section heads in sentence case.

title.purpose: Facts, room names, the wall heading slip.

label.purpose: Buttons, tabs, nav: condensed bold caps.

micro.purpose: Pitch bar, field labels, swatch meta.

mark-a.purpose: Cinzel redraw of the existing VIA mark; Logo Option A only.

shadows.name: paste
shadows.purpose: Default for every pasted sheet: posters, buttons, room cards, photo slots, remnants.

shadows.name: strip
shadows.purpose: The booking strip inside the lead poster.

shadows.name: ghost-edge
shadows.purpose: Ghost button printed edge (3px on hover).

shadows.name: paste-seam
shadows.purpose: Overlap line where a sheet is glued over the next (defined, field--pasted; not currently applied in pages).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The single house ease for every transition and keyframe.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: .9s ease-out, stagger 90ms; from rotate(tilt*3) translateY(10px) scale(1.015)
motion.purpose: Posters arrive visible and settle onto the wall.

motion.name: brush
motion.value: 1.1s ease-out, delay index*90ms + 120ms; sheen translateX(-120%) to 120%
motion.purpose: One paste-brush sweep across each poster.

motion.name: tab-tear
motion.value: transform .45s ease-out; translateY(14px) rotate(-5deg..5deg); navigate after 320ms

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: all durations .01ms, animations none; JS skips the tear

narrative.northStar: Affissioni, the Poster Wall on Shrewsbury Street
narrative.overview:
VIA's site is an Italian billposting wall. The page background is plaster (muro); every offer, event, menu and room is a sheet of drenched poster stock pasted onto it, edge to edge or slightly askew, with a seam of wall showing between sheets. The craft reference is mid-century Italian poster work (Depero, Olivetti, Pirelli): flat fields of brick, olive, saffron and Super Tuscan plum, huge expanded black type, and a small vocabulary of cut-paper shapes that each stand for something real at VIA (the fire, the plate, the spit, the glass, the deal, the table).

The wall is honest about time. Every poster carries its dates first, and the code takes a poster down the day after its `data-end` date (Worcester time). An expired poster can leave a muro-deep remnant ("Was Tue, Jun 16 · pasted over"). Actions are not floating buttons but tear-off tabs cut along the poster's bottom edge, like a street flyer; pressing one tears it before the link follows. Photography is pasted on like a clipping, tilted, never full-bleed behind type; until VIA supplies photos, every photo is a labelled, hatched slot naming the shot and ratio.

Density is poster-scale: few words, very large, set in one family (Archivo) used across its width axis the way a printer uses wood type. The system deliberately refuses the restaurant category default it replaces (the old viaitaliantable.com look and its peers): a dark full-bleed food photo, a gold serif, and a lone "Reserve" button. Gold survives only inside Logo Option A.
keyCharacteristics: Whole fields of colour, never thin accents; colour is what a poster is made of.
One typeface, Archivo, across widths: 125 to shout, 112 for headlines, 70 to 85 for labels and dates, 100 to read.
Square-cut rectangles and whole cut-paper curves; nothing in between.
Depth is paper on plaster: a paste shadow and a hair of rotation, no cards, no glass.
Dates lead, expired content disappears, and the three doors (book, order, plan an event) are one tap from anywhere.
Two switchable identities (A: existing gold mark; B: cut-paper VIA wordmark) inside the same poster world.

rules.name: The Drenched Field Rule
rules.body: Colour comes as whole poster fields, never as a thin accent stripe or tinted card. A typical page by area runs roughly mattone 24%, muro 20%, oliva 16%, prugna 14%, ink 14%, zafferano 12%.

rules.name: The Ink-or-Paper Rule
rules.body: Text on mattone, oliva and prugna is paper (#fbf6ee); text on zafferano, bianco and muro is ink. Paper on saffron (2.0:1) and ink on brick (2.8:1) fail and are never used for text. Measured pairs: paper on mattone 6.0:1, paper on oliva 6.8:1, paper on prugna 13.9:1, ink on saffron 8.4:1, mattone on bianco 5.6:1.

rules.name: The Gold Belongs to A Rule
rules.body: Oro appears only inside Logo Option A, always on an ink or plum ground. The new world never borrows gold.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo is the only typeface of the world. Contrast comes from the width axis (125 / 112 / 100 / 85 / 70) and weight, never from a second display face. Cinzel exists only as Logo A's placeholder.

rules.name: The Date Leads Rule
rules.body: On any poster the bold date (start or end) is the first line of text, then the kind of thing it is, in small type: "Tuesday, Dec 8 · 6:30 pm · Wine dinner". A poster with no end date says so ("For a limited time", "Any night").

rules.name: The Name, Not a Slogan Rule
rules.body: Poster type sets the name of the thing (PigFest, Whole suckling pig, $25 entrées), never a tagline.

rules.name: The Three Doors Rule
rules.body: Book (Resy), order (Toast / DoorDash) and plan an event (private dining / Tripleseat) are reachable in one tap from every page: masthead Book button and nav on wide screens, the fixed action bar on phones, and the lead poster's strip and doors on home.

rules.name: The Pasted, Not Floating Rule
rules.body: Every raised element uses the paste shadow and stays square to the wall or tilted by under 1deg (photo clippings up to about 2.2deg). Nothing hovers with a large diffuse glow.

dos: Do build every offer, event and special as a poster with the five-part anatomy: art band, dates, title, body, tear-off tabs.
Do give every time-limited poster a `data-end` date so it comes down by itself, and say "For a limited time" or "Any night" when there is no end date.
Do fill whole fields with a poster stock (mattone, oliva, zafferano, prugna, ink) and keep bianco for set-text surfaces: masthead, menus, forms, booking fields.
Do set paper type (#fbf6ee) on mattone, oliva, prugna and ink, and ink type on zafferano, bianco and muro.
Do use Archivo only, varying width: 125 for poster type, 112 for headlines, 70 to 85 for labels, dates and actions, 100 for reading.
Do keep rectangles square-cut and use curves only as whole cut-paper circles and half-discs from the six shapes.
Do paste sheets with the paste shadow (`0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.06), 0 10px 24px -14px rgba(28,21,18,.55)`) and a tilt under 1deg.
Do keep book, order and plan-an-event one tap away on every page.
Do put photos in labelled slots, pasted like clippings, with the shot and ratio named.
donts: Don't fall back to the category default this world replaces: a dark full-bleed food photo with a gold serif and a lone "Reserve" button.
Don't set text over a photo or a cut-paper shape; shapes live in the art band, photos in slots.
Don't use gold (oro) or Cinzel anywhere outside Logo Option A.
Don't put paper type on saffron (2.0:1) or ink type on brick (2.8:1).
Don't add gradients, outlines or textures to cut-paper shapes, or put more than three shapes in one poster.
Don't round the corners of posters, buttons, tabs or fields.
Don't stretch, outline or shadow Logo B, recolour its sun beyond saffron (or brick on saffron), or mix Options A and B in one piece.
Don't let a promotion linger past its date or show a poster before its start date.
